meta.desc.index: Gitflow lab for the mini-course: long-lived branches, release cycle, tags and changelog.
meta.desc.docs: Quick guide to the Gitflow workflow used in this mini-course: commands, PR targets and the release cycle.
hero.sub: The lab on the other side of the comparison. Here nothing goes straight to main: all work goes through develop, becomes a release/*, gets a tag and only then is published.
modelo.intro: Two branches live forever (main and develop). The others are born, fulfil a role and die. The path from an idea to production necessarily goes through all of them.
modelo.svg.titulo: Gitflow diagram: a feature branches off develop, returns to develop, enters a release branch and is published to main with a tag
branches.titulo: What branches from where, and what returns to where
branches.intro: This table is the rule of the game in this repository. Picking the wrong Pull Request target is the most common mistake for people starting with Gitflow.
branches.main: Always reflects what is published. Every commit here has a tag.
branches.develop: Where the team's work accumulates until it forms the next version.
branches.feature: One task. Never talks to main directly.
branches.release: Freeze scope, adjust version and changelog, fix the last details.
branches.hotfix: Production emergency, without waiting for the next release.
release.intro: Compare it mentally with the trunk-based repository: there, publishing is git push. Here there are six steps — and this is exactly the cost you need to feel in order to decide when it is worth it.
release.p1.texto: release/1.1.0 is created from develop. From here on, no new feature enters this version.
release.p2.texto: VERSION and CHANGELOG.md are updated on the release branch.
release.p3.texto: Only fixes go in. Each one is also taken back to develop.
release.p4.texto: Merge into main → the deploy Action puts the version online.
release.p5.texto: A v1.1.0 tag and a GitHub Release are created automatically from the CHANGELOG.
release.p6.texto: Back-merge from main to develop, so the fix is not lost in the next version.
participantes.intro: Same pattern as the trunk-based repository: one file per person in data/participantes/. What changes here is not the file — it is the path it takes to go live.
participantes.vazio: Nobody here yet — be the first person to add a file in data/participantes/.

contribuir.nota: Your commit only shows up on the site when the next version is published — and that is a characteristic of the model, not a defect. Details in CONTRIBUTING.md.
docs.sub: Enough to work in this repository without picking the wrong Pull Request target.
docs.r1.texto: main is what is published; develop is what will be published. Everything else is temporary and must be deleted after the merge.
docs.r2.titulo: 2. You never commit directly to main or develop
docs.r2.texto: Always from a feature/*, with a Pull Request. Both permanent branches are protected — direct pushes are rejected by GitHub.
docs.r3.titulo: 3. The PR target depends on where the branch came from
docs.r3.texto: feature/* → develop. release/* and hotfix/* → main, and then back to develop. CI rejects the PR if the target is wrong.
docs.r4.titulo: 4. A version is a decision, not a consequence
docs.r4.texto: The number in VERSION only changes inside a release/* or hotfix/* branch. Your feature never touches it — it touches CHANGELOG.md, in the Unreleased section.
docs.r5.titulo: 5. What went into main must return to develop
docs.r5.texto: Fixes made in a release or hotfix need the back-merge, otherwise they reappear as a bug in the next version. Here that becomes an automatic PR.
docs.doeu.intro: Keep these observations for the final discussion of the mini-course — they are the material for the comparison with the trunk-based repository:
docs.q1: How much time passed between your commit and it showing up on the site?
docs.q2: How many steps did it take to publish a one-line change?
docs.q3: Did your branch conflict? How many days old was it?
docs.q4: On the upside: could you say exactly which version contains each change?
docs.q5: And could you roll the whole site back to a previous version with one command?
erro404.titulo: This page didn't make it into the release
erro404.sub: The address you looked for does not exist in this published version. Maybe it is still on develop, waiting for the next cycle.
